newsitem.title: USA: Sen. Lott aide offers Navy contract changes - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Sen. Lott aide offers Navy contract changes - WSJ.

text.p: Pentagon officials received a list of demands by an aide of Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott regarding handling of the U.S. Navy's shipbuilding contracts, the Wall Street Journal said on Wednesday.
If met, the page-long list would cause large changes in the U.S. shipbuilding industry, the paper said in its electronic edition.

According to people on Capitol Hill and in the Pentagon, the list was brought to meetings by Lott staffer Eric Womble, the newspaper said. Lott's office was quoted as declining to comment on the report and the Journal said Womble did not return calls looking for comment.

Most of the proposed changes would move business to Ingalls shipbuilding yard, a Litton Industries unit in Lott's homestate of Mississippi, from other private and public shipyards, the newspaper said.
The list requested giving Ingalls at least two and maybe four more contracts to build DDG-51 destroyers, which each cost about $750 million, the paper said.
It also called for adding two more of the destroyers to the Navy's shipbuilding plants, the newspaper said.
